glosses: to grant

examples.text: дарова́ть проще́ние кому́-либо
дарова́ть кому́-либо свобо́ду (жизнь)

glosses: устар., высок. наградить кого-то чем-то

examples.text: Даровать шубу с царского плеча.

glosses: перен. в сочетании со словами жизнь, свобода и т. п. — подарить

examples.text: Даровать преступнику помилование.

glosses: To give (permission or wish).

examples.text: He was granted permission to attend the meeting.
The genie granted him three wishes

glosses: To give (bestow upon or confer, particularly in answer to prayer or request).

examples.text: He Suſpends on theſe Reaſons, that Thomas Rue had granted a general Diſcharge to Adam Muſhet, who was his Conjunct, and correus debendi, after the alleadged Service, which Diſcharged Muſhet, and conſequently Houstoun his Partner.

c. 1930, Serenity Prayer
God, grant me the serenity[…]
In order to grant the rich these pleasures, the social contract is reconfigured. The welfare state is dismantled. […]

glosses: To agree with (someone) on (something); to accept (something) for the sake of argument; to admit to (someone) that (something) is true.

examples.text: The universe exists, said the father: somebody must have made it. If that somebody exists, said I, somebody must have made him. I grant that for the sake of argument, said the Oratorian.

"They are tall, certainly," said Sir Chetwynd... "I grant you they are tall. That is, the majority of them are. But I have seen short men among them. The Khedive is not taller than I am. And the Egyptian face is very deceptive. The features are often fine,—occasionally classic,—but intelligent expression is totally lacking."

glosses: To assent; to consent.

examples.text:
Before I would have granted to that act.
But thou preferr'st thy life before thine honor.

glosses: The act of granting or giving

examples.text: the grant of permission for a project

glosses: The yielding or admission of something in dispute.
The thing or property granted; a gift; a boon.

examples.text: I got a grant from the government to study archeology in Egypt.

glosses: A transfer of property by deed or writing; especially, an appropriation or conveyance made by the government.

examples.text: a grant of land or of money

glosses: The deed or writing by which such a transfer is made.
An application for a grant (monetary boon to aid research or the like).
To grant as a possession; to bestow.

examples.text:
Nor shall I count in hainous to enjoy
The public marks of honour and reward
 Conferr'd upon me[…]
The college has conferred an honorary degree upon the visiting Prime Minister.
Abel tried to refuse the honor thus unexpectedly conferred upon him, but it was no use. He had been made a deacon, and a deacon he must remain.
The special immunities that are conferred on MPs were framed with the essential purpose of allowing them to speak freely in parliament.
The mere existence of a dictionary of a certain variety of English does not automatically confer acceptance of that variety.

glosses: To talk together, to consult, discuss; to collogue.

examples.text: They were in a huddle, conferring about something.
Local buttons popped when Henry Kissinger visited Little Rock last month to confer with Fulbright on the Middle East oil talks.

glosses: To compare.

examples.text: The Newe Testament ... Conferred diligently with the Greke, and best approued translations.
Confer thine estate with others […]. Be content and rest satisfied, for thou art well in respect to others […].
If we confer these observations with others of the like nature, we may find cause to rectify the general opinion.

glosses: To bring together; to collect, gather.
To contribute; to conduce.

examples.text: The closeness and compactness of the parts resting together doth much confer to the strength of the union.

glosses: jemandem etwas ohne Entgelt geben, das er behalten kann

examples.text: Sie schenkte ihm zum Geburtstag ein Buch.
„Die Portiers schenken mir Briefmarken, die ich sammle, weil ich sie vielleicht später verkaufen kann.“

glosses: jemandem etwas zuteilwerden lassen, jemandem etwas geben

examples.text: Das Buch hat ihm neuen Lebensmut geschenkt.
Nach tagelangem Warten schenkten sie ihm Aufmerksamkeit.
Nachdem das Kitz wieder gesund geworden war, schenkten wir ihm die Freiheit.

glosses: jemandem etwas ersparen

examples.text: Im Sportunterricht hat der Lehrer uns heute den lästigen 3000-Meter-Lauf geschenkt.
Gisa wird auf der Arbeit nichts geschenkt.

glosses: ein Getränk ausschenken, anbieten

examples.text: Bei der Gala schenkte man einen edlen Rotwein.

glosses: ein Getränk in ein Gefäß eingießen, einschenken

examples.text: Er schenkte den Tee in die Tassen.

glosses: sich etwas sparen, auf etwas verzichten

examples.text: Die Mühe kannst du dir schenken, ich habe schon alles gemacht.
Die Fahrt hierher hättest du dir schenken können, denn es sind alle Veranstaltungen abgesagt worden.

glosses: Donner, accorder.
